page_definition: gold_page = unit number inside the document (unit id <document_id>#uNN), see data/manifest.json
selection_rule_fixed_before_test: Choose the strategy with the highest dev Evidence Hit@3; ties -> higher dev Hit@1; then fewer chunks / lower ingest time. Test is evaluated once after the choice is fixed.

questions.question: How many spaces should be used for each indentation level in Python code?
questions.expected_answer: 4 spaces per indentation level.
questions.evidence_quote: Use 4 spaces per indentation level.

questions.question: What is the maximum line length recommended by the Python style guide?
questions.expected_answer: 79 characters for all lines.
questions.evidence_quote: Limit all lines to a maximum of 79 characters.

questions.question: When a long arithmetic expression is split over several lines in new code, should the line break go before or after the plus and minus signs?
questions.expected_answer: Before the binary operator (Knuth's style) for new code; either is permitted if consistent locally.
questions.evidence_quote: In Python code, it is permissible to break before or after a binary operator, as long as the convention is consistent locally.  For new code Knuth's style is suggested.

questions.question: Should I use == to check whether a variable is None?
questions.expected_answer: No; comparisons to singletons like None should use is / is not, never equality operators.
questions.evidence_quote: Comparisons to singletons like None should always be done with is or is not, never the equality operators.

questions.question: In which order should the different groups of import statements be arranged at the top of a module?
questions.expected_answer: Standard library, then related third party, then local application/library specific imports.
questions.evidence_quote:
1. Standard library imports.
  2. Related third party imports.
  3. Local application/library specific imports.

questions.question: For a one-line docstring, where should the closing triple quotes be placed?
questions.expected_answer: On the same line as the opening quotes.
questions.evidence_quote: The closing quotes are on the same line as the opening quotes.

questions.question: Can I use a backslash inside the braces of an f-string expression, for example to escape a quote?
questions.expected_answer: No; backslashes may not appear inside the expression portions of f-strings.
questions.evidence_quote: Backslashes may not appear inside the expression portions of f-strings

questions.question: When are adjacent f-strings concatenated compared with adjacent regular string literals?
questions.expected_answer: Regular strings at compile time, f-strings at run time.
questions.evidence_quote: Regular strings are concatenated at compile time, and f-strings are concatenated at run time.

questions.question: Which exception is raised when you try to set an attribute on a frozen dataclass instance?
questions.expected_answer: FrozenInstanceError (raised by the added __setattr__/__delattr__).
questions.evidence_quote: In that case, Data Classes will add __setattr__ and __delattr__ methods to the class.  These methods will raise a FrozenInstanceError when invoked.

questions.question: What happens if a dataclass field is given an empty list as its default value?
questions.expected_answer: A TypeError is raised for list, dict or set defaults.
questions.evidence_quote: Data Classes will raise a TypeError if it detects a default parameter of type list, dict, or set.

questions.question: Is it valid to write y := f(x) as a statement on its own line without parentheses?
questions.expected_answer: No; unparenthesized assignment expressions are prohibited at the top level of an expression statement.
questions.evidence_quote: Unparenthesized assignment expressions are prohibited at the top level of an expression statement.

questions.question: Can the walrus target reuse the loop variable of the comprehension, as in [i := i+1 for i in range(5)]?
questions.expected_answer: No; the target cannot be the same as a for-target name of a containing comprehension (it is invalid / SyntaxError).
questions.evidence_quote: an assignment expression target name cannot be the same as a for-target name appearing in any comprehension containing the assignment expression.

questions.question: How do I write a catch-all case that matches anything when no other pattern matched?
questions.filter_context: User is reading the Informational tutorial material (assumed input provided before retrieval).
questions.expected_answer: Use the wildcard pattern _ as the last case; it always matches and binds no variable.
questions.evidence_quote: This special pattern which is written _ (and called wildcard) always matches but it doesn't bind any variables.

questions.question: What error do I get when iterating over zip with strict=True and the inputs have different lengths?
questions.filter_context: User targets Python 3.10 features (assumed input provided before retrieval).
questions.expected_answer: ValueError when the arguments are exhausted at differing lengths.
questions.evidence_quote: When the built-in zip is called with the keyword-only argument strict=True, the resulting iterator will raise a ValueError if the arguments are exhausted at differing lengths.

questions.question: If the guard expression of a case block raises an exception, what happens?
questions.filter_context: User wants the normative specification, i.e. Standards Track PEPs (assumed input provided before retrieval).
questions.expected_answer: The guard is evaluated after the patterns succeed; if it raises, the exception bubbles up.
questions.evidence_quote: If a guard is present on a case block, once the pattern or patterns in the case block succeed, the expression in the guard is evaluated.  If this raises an exception, the exception bubbles up.

questions.question: Can I call isinstance with a parameterized generic such as list[str] as the second argument?
questions.expected_answer: No; it raises TypeError: isinstance() arg 2 cannot be a parameterized generic.
questions.evidence_quote: TypeError: isinstance() arg 2 cannot be a parameterized generic

questions.question: What naming convention should class names follow?
questions.expected_answer: CapWords (with a noted exception for callables documented like functions).
questions.evidence_quote: Class names should normally use the CapWords convention.

questions.question: How can each new dataclass object get its own fresh list instead of sharing one default list?
questions.expected_answer: Use field(default_factory=list); the factory is called with zero arguments whenever a default is needed.
questions.evidence_quote: If a field specifies a default_factory, it is called with zero arguments when a default value for the field is needed.

alternative_gold.evidence_quote: default_factory: If provided, it must be a zero-argument callable that will be called when a default value is needed for this field.

questions.question: Is an f-string a constant value or is it evaluated when the program runs?
questions.expected_answer: It is an expression evaluated at run time, not a constant value.
questions.evidence_quote: an f-string is really an expression evaluated at run time, not a constant value.

questions.question: Can an assignment expression be used inside an f-string replacement field without parentheses?
questions.expected_answer: No; inside f-strings assignment expressions require parentheses (f'{x:=10}' is parsed as a format spec).
questions.evidence_quote: Assignment expressions inside of f-strings require parentheses.

questions.question: How can I annotate a value that may be an int or None without importing Optional?
questions.filter_context: User targets Python 3.10 features (assumed input provided before retrieval).
questions.expected_answer: Write int | None (t | None or None | t) instead of Optional[t].
questions.evidence_quote: We will also be able to write t | None or None | t instead of Optional[t]

questions.question: How should a docstring that spans several lines be structured?
questions.expected_answer: A one-line summary, then a blank line, then a more elaborate description.
questions.evidence_quote: Multi-line docstrings consist of a summary line just like a one-line docstring, followed by a blank line, followed by a more elaborate description.
